newsitem.title: USA: Clinton attacks fashion industry image of heroin.
newsitem.headline: Clinton attacks fashion industry image of heroin.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton on Wednesday accused the fashion industry of projecting a positive image of heroin use and said it should not try to "glamorize addiction to sell clothes."
Addressing a U.S. Conference of Mayors forum on drug abuse, Clinton cited the fashion industry for "increasing the allure of heroin among young people."

"We now see on college campuses and in neighbourhoods heroin becoming increasingly the drug of choice," Clinton told the mayors. "And we know that part of this has to do with the images that are finding their way to our young people."

"Our society cannot say on the one hand we want to have a tough intolerant attitude toward drugs, and on the other hand send a very different message every time there might be a little money to be made on it," Clinton said.
He was attacking the so-called "heroin chic" approach that has been used in some fashion photography, in which models pose dazed as if under the influence of drugs.

Some fashion leaders were "admitting flat out that images projected in fashion photos in the last few years have made heroin addiction seem glamorous and sexy and cool," Clinton said. "As some of the people in those images start to die now, it becomes obvious that that is not true. You do not need to glamorize addition to sell clothes."
